title: Chapter 4: Workplace Hazards and Accident Prevention

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Workplace hazards are classified into five main types: Physical, Chemical, Biological, Ergonomic, and Psychological hazards.
Accidents result from two main primary factors: Unsafe Acts by personnel and Unsafe Conditions within the work environment.
The 3 E's of accident prevention comprise Engineering Controls, Education/Training, and Enforcement of rules.
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) represents the final line of defense in the hazard control hierarchy.
The Hierarchy of Hazard Controls prioritizes Elimination, Substitution, Engineering Controls, Administrative Controls, and PPE.

blocks.content: A workplace hazard is any condition, situation, or activity that has the potential to cause injury, illness, or damage to workers, equipment, or the environment. In workshops and industrial settings, workers are often exposed to machines, electricity, chemicals, heat, noise, and heavy materials. If hazards are not properly identified and controlled, they can lead to serious accidents.
Accident prevention involves identifying hazards, controlling risks, following safety rules, and ensuring that workers are properly trained to perform their tasks safely.

An accident is an unplanned and unexpected event that results in injury, damage to property, or loss of life. In technical workshops, accidents may occur due to unsafe behavior, unsafe working conditions, or lack of proper knowledge about equipment and safety procedures.
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) serves as the last line of defense against workplace hazards.

blocks.content: Safety awareness programs and training sessions help workers understand workplace hazards and learn how to avoid accidents. Regular safety meetings, demonstrations, and safety drills improve workers' knowledge and preparedness.

items: Distinguish between Direct Costs (compensation, medical care) and Indirect Costs (lost production time, equipment damage, training replacement workers) in accident cost evaluations.

Memorize the correct sequence of the Hierarchy of Hazard Controls from most effective (Elimination) to least effective (PPE).
